en: If we charge in, we will seize it.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
We shall bring slaughter upon China.
Such was the testament that was made,
This is what the ear heard.
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
There is the Heaven-khan in Beijing.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Go and declare your grievance before them.
You have many words already spoken,
In Chañu, which was laid waste,
At the corner where corrupt words were uttered,
You have a name that can bring ruin.
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
If you grow wrathful, you will prevail,
If you refuse the words that are spoken,
If they will not walk the road appointed,
The great people of Beijing,
When the warrior speaks in anger,
If you lash the world onward,
Look upon it and act,
You have put it to the test; know this.
Take the word of Heaven from abroad,
He gained the land without making a raid,
He took the people who had been overrun,
The nation’s inherited wealth is a tethering stake,
Heroism requires a people,
To range abroad requires land.
The people are dear, the nation is a pledge,
What the ear has heard and the eye has seen,
We shall divide it as an inheritance for the people.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
All of the wide world,
You will see gathered together.
Saying this, Zhan Zhetpes continued,
Saying that he had become a sovereign in peace.
One from each and every people,
Saying, “Appoint one from among the envoys,”
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Saying, “Let Chyng Temir be the padishah,”
Send an envoy between us,
Without clashing or quarreling,
Take counsel and testimony from the people.
If you clash and quarrel,
His valor is not greater than the people’s,
Your thunder is not so great,
Do not turn this into a reckless affair,
What I have said to you is no great thing.
Bow to one who bows,
He is one of a heroic people,
They are a people who know cultivation,
My lord, his road and passage are open,
He is one of a heroic people.
From one who stands as a shield for the people,
Whose forefathers were heroes,
One who takes his stand beneath the banner.
What can excuse the multitude,
Who led a people as vast as a multitude,
Is hardship the fault of the sword,
From your eye that sees the distant target,
From one who foresees the people's fate,
Closing our eyes and saying that God will come,
If he should see it by chance,
If he acts rudely without warning,
The true banner named by Tengir,
Saying he will see it above the house.
Let us set out far, far away,
Let us remain and draw close,
Bulls, rams, and camels of every sort,
Let us name the fine ones we behold.
Let us measure him carefully and make him rue it,
Seeing the raven of power,
The finest knower of stratagems,
Again came the wise man’s words,
Thinking with cunning and working your scheme,
Making your false words seem fitting,
It seems you remained defending them,
The stock of the Kara Kyrgyz,
It seems you remained praising them.
You went about with this lie in China,
It seems you intended to give it away,
When the people of China heard it,
You yourself, at the root of it all,
It seems you called it their land,
The force of your words made it overflow.
You are this roving eye of the Kyrgyz.
The work you carried on from its root,
You saw it whole from its appearance.
Weighing your wits concerning the Kyrgyz,
It seems you called it their foundation,
For these Kyrgyz—not merely China—
It seems you called it their land.
You went about ruining the people,
This envoy of the Kakanchi,
It seems you intended to leave.
Your manner is that of one who ruins a people,
Your form is that of a black scourge,
You are one of the thousands beyond counting,
If you stand there sprawling and abandon it,
Your blame will settle upon the Kyrgyz.
If you make Beijing ring out,
Speaking your truth without reserve,
Finding its inside with your hand,
If you make your hand a servant,
From Kyrgyz to Kyrgyz,
The envoy of the Kyrgyz.
Outwardly, your enemy is black,
Your ruined secret is what you destroyed,
You have thrown my people into ruin.
Jeljetpes stood there in anguish,
Lowering his face and yielding,
This vain world is faithless,
Its falseness became known,
Taking truth itself for falsehood,
After the khan poured out his wrath,
Was there any khan who could answer back?
From Tengir’s battle cry and venom,
My thought that has no equal,
Returning again to the true matter,
Grief-stricken and sorrowful,
With no other thought left to pursue,
There stood Jeljetpes.
Lamenting, his eyes shone,
His care divided into countless cares,
Chyng Temir, whose wrath was hell,
Appeared in a fearsome aspect,
Though one begged, no life would be spared,
Though one pleaded, none would remain.
Born of a father and mother,
What created mortal does not die?
You steeped its writing in blood,
Why would my heart not fear?
The garment that came into your hand,
I struck down the fierce ones you saw,
For God and for the people,
I will bind your head to misery.
I am not dead; I am alive,
If hostile death reaches me, let me die.
The khan’s command is precious,
Let me tell the truth.
Of the brave white-kalpak Kyrgyz people,
Let me tell their secret.
If this head bows, will it not die?
Can warmed-over humiliation protect anyone?
For its elders to remain whole,
How much hardship falls to the hero,
Before the black eye of the scourge,
To the hell created for him,
Speaking my verse with a cry,
Telling my truth as faithfully as belief,
Of the brave white-kalpak Kyrgyz people,
Who destroyed six generations of this one’s fathers,
From this father came the lionhearted people’s spirit,
Let me tell their secret.
For true speech and for the secret,
For the quarrel between the two peoples,
Let me die at the hands of the wrathful one.
Speaking heatedly, Zhelzhetpes,
The accomplished Kyrgyz spoke out.
Below lay the people within China,
He was one of the true brave men,
Of all things and of unity,
Waging war with his weapons,
Tormenting with death,
The bad and the good,
Of heat and cold.
He was a man who understood what was plain to see.
A great people guarded by a mighty fortress,
Clear-eyed in this world,
Even if he died, his eyes would remain open,
This Zhelzhetpes was a heroic warrior,
They would call him a true saint.
He sharpened his eloquent tongue,
He paused and sharpened it once again,
Then Zhelzhetpes spoke out.
At thirty, he himself was an eloquent hero,
The Kenens who guarded every land,
A sage eloquent in speech,
Coming out ahead in the contest,
The land of China is no lesser,
Among the people there is an impartial judge,
Who addressed the forty tribes,
From the common Kyrgyz people,
His words and his tongue were golden,
Do not rage or pour out your wrath,
On this side lies their blue-gray expanse,
They possess freedom like a towering blue mountain,
Among the Kyrgyz there is Khan Kenen.
Unless you cast it before the multitude,
If Tengir himself appears before you,
He has the strength to stand against you.
Though your people are many,
The few Kyrgyz are no falsehood,
If we gauge their strength and tell the secret,
You bellowed as though struck down,
My khan, what you have done is not right.
A khan’s command is an iron snare,
When you rage and stiffen in anger,
Our misery begins to boil.
Going to the truthful one and speaking truth,
Our misery has boiled over.
There is much weeping in the breast,
Let his jester make it grand,
There is a god over your rough shoe,
For solid iron there is an axe,
There is deceit within your rough shoe.
That wise man knew the calamity,
If you are a shallow-witted khan,
Hang it from this neck of mine,
He spoke piercingly and defended it,
Speaking of what he saw and knew,
One who brings them safely through,
The white-kalpak people are not an easy people,
Having Karman’s head cut off,
I am not one who stands in your hand.
When the khan’s age comes, cry out,
I am not one who stands in your hand,
Saying, “You revealed the enemy’s secret,”
This deed of yours is not manly.
You cursed him for speaking the truth,
If you make strife, its blow will reach you,
If you rage and stiffen in anger,
You will see it brought to submission.
Your folly will become your affliction.
Know it clearly and keep it in mind,
The heart that was to be driven,
Will the mind comprehend it?
He spoke out when telling the truth,
Yourself, fine as a thread in the true secret,
Now you have troubled my sight,
The ruling khan suffered,
I have no guilt and no strength,
The people clamored and an uproar arose,
The brave soul asked,
If you see wrongdoing among the people,
This will become cause for outcry,
Remain without inflicting suffering,
You are a twin to the envoy.
Warrior, you are peerless and without equal,
You have burning force and flame,
You have wise men and companions,
You have eloquent men who find wise counsel,
Your champion Akbala,
Suradai spoke; understand this.
Your ancient forefather was a great khan,
Warrior Chyng Tengir, understand this.
The four eshens share one root,
If you cut its nose, there is no milk,
The horned foe is a companion of the soul,
There is no day when the thoroughbred fails,
Jeljetpes who stands in your hand,
If you strike the innocent, you will not prosper,
You will stir up a madness best left alone,
Scattering wrath, you rule the people,
You will not prosper for a long age.
